en: Unvarying; all the same.
Consistent; conforming to one standard.
A distinctive outfit that serves to identify members of a group, company, prison inmates, etc.
A uniformed police officer (as opposed to a detective).
To clothe in a uniform.

uniform.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ís?
Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos
Proto-Italic *oinos
Old Latin oinos
Latin ūnus
Latin ūni-
Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ)der.?
Latin fōrma
Latin -fōrmis
Latin uniformis
Middle French uniformebor.
English uniform
Borrowed from Middle French uniforme, from Latin uniformis.

ex.en: The new houses are of a uniform height.
ex.ja: それらの新築の家はみな同じ高さである。

ex.en: Our school did away with uniforms last year.
ex.ja: 私たちの学校は昨年制服を廃止した。

ex.en: Team members are provided with equipment and uniforms.
ex.ja: チームのメンバーは道具とユニフォームを提供されます。

note.ja: uni（1つ）+ form（形）。1つの形の →「制服・一様な」。

en: undomesticated animals, especially mammals, birds, and fish, which live in the wild.
Living undomesticated organisms of all kinds.

wildlife.ety:
Etymology tree
English wild
Proto-Indo-European *leyp-der.
Proto-Germanic *lībanąder.
Proto-Germanic *lībą
Proto-West Germanic *līb
Old English līf
Middle English lyf
English life
English wildlife
From wild + life.

ex.en: The organization plays a principal role in wildlife conservation.
ex.ja: その団体は野生動物の保護において、最も重要な役割を果たしている。

ex.en: The area is notable for its scenery and wildlife.
ex.ja: その地域は風景と野生動物で注目に値する。

en: Made of wood.
As if made of wood; moving awkwardly, or speaking with dull lack of emotion.

wooden.ety:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From wood + -en. Dates from 1530s, gradually replaced treen (“made from a tree”), from Middle English treen, from Old English triewen.

ex.en: I'd rather live in a wooden house.
ex.ja: どちらかといえば木造住宅に住みたい。

ex.en: A wooden building can easily catch fire.
ex.ja: 木造家屋は簡単に燃える。

ex.en: An old wooden box served as table.
ex.ja: 古い木箱がテーブルの役目をした。

en: Characterized by aggression; highly combative; prone to behave in a way that involves attacking (especially if unjustly) or arguing.
Tends to attack the player while unprovoked.
One who is aggressive.
A (Black) woman who presents as masculine; a butch.

aggressive.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd
Proto-Italic *ad
Proto-Italic *ad-
Latin ad-
Proto-Indo-European *gʰredʰ-der.
Latin gradior
Latin aggredior
Latin aggressuslbor.
English aggress
Proto-Indo-European *-wós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.
Latin -īvus
Old French -ifbor.
Middle English -yf
English -ive
English aggressive
From aggress + -ive. Compare with French agressif.

ex.en: He is so aggressive that others avoid him.
ex.ja: 彼はあまりにも性格が攻撃的で、人に避けられている。

ex.en: He assumed an aggressive attitude toward me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に攻撃的な態度をとった。

ex.en: You have to be aggressive to be a success.
ex.ja: 出世するためには積極的な人間でなければならない。

note.ja: ag（〜へ）+ gress（歩む）+ ive。〜へ攻め寄る →「攻撃的な・積極的な」。

en: Capable of being seen, or easily seen; open to view; visible to the eye; within sight or view.
Clear or manifest to the understanding; plain; evident; obvious; known; palpable; indubitable.

apparent.ety: From Middle English apparaunt, aparaunt, from Old French aparent, aparant, in turn from Latin appārēns, appārentis, present participle of appāreō.

ex.en: It is apparent that he will win the election.
ex.ja: 彼が選挙で勝利を収めるのは明らかだ。

ex.en: His apparent anger proved to be only a joke.
ex.ja: 彼は腹を立てた様子だったが、結局それは冗談だった。

ex.en: The apparent truth was really a lie.
ex.ja: その一見真実らしいことは実は嘘だった。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ pare（見える）+ nt。目の前に見えている →「明らかな・見かけの」。appear（現れる）。

en: A sudden percussive noise.
A heavy strike upon an object causing such a noise.
To make sudden loud noises, often repeatedly, especially by exploding or hitting something.
To hit (something) hard, making a loud noise.
Right, directly.
Precisely, exactly, completely.
A sudden percussive sound, such as made by the firing of a gun, slamming of a door, etc.

bang.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *bangōną
Old English *bangian
Old Norse bangabor.
Middle English *bangen
English bang
From Middle English *bangen, from Old English *bangian or borrowed from Old Norse banga (“to pound, hammer”); both from Proto-Germanic *bangōną (“to beat, pound”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰen- (“to beat, hit, injure”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots bang, bung (“to strike, bang, hurl, thrash, offend”), Icelandic banga (“to pound, hammer”), Old Swedish bånga ("to hammer"; whence modern Swedish banka (“to knock, pound, bang”)), Danish banke (“to beat”), bengel (“club”), Low German

ex.en: I got a bang out of her party.
ex.ja: 彼女のパーティーは実に楽しかった。

ex.en: He banged a big book on the desk.
ex.ja: 彼は大きな本をドスンと机の上に置いた。

ex.en: The car banged itself against a tree.
ex.ja: 車がどしんと木にぶつかった。

en: A violent gust of wind (in windy weather) or apparent wind (around a moving vehicle).
A forcible stream of gas or liquid from an orifice, for example from a bellows, the tuyeres of a blast furnace, a person's mouth, etc.
To make an impression on, by making a loud blast or din.
To make a loud noise.
Used to show anger or disappointment: damn

blast.ety:
Inherited from Middle English blast, from Old English blǣst (“blowing, blast”), from Proto-West Germanic *blāstu, from Proto-Germanic *blēstuz (“blowing, blast”).
Cognate with West Frisian blast (“blast”), dialectal Dutch blast (“stubborn intent, drumming”), obsolete German Blast (“wind, blowing”), German blasen (“to blow”), Dutch blazen (“to blow”), Danish blæst (“wind”), French blaser (“to blunt, dull”). More at blow.

ex.en: You have to blast your way out.
ex.ja: 人垣をかき分けて出なくちゃね。

ex.en: A lot of people were killed by the blast.
ex.ja: 多くの人が爆発で死んだ。

ex.en: The blast-off took place on schedule.
ex.ja: ロケットの発射は予定通り行なわれた。

zh: 共產主義者 /共产主义者

en: Of, relating to, supporting, or advocating communism.
An advocate of a society based on the common ownership of property; a proponent of communism.

communist.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *mey-
Proto-Indo-European *ḱom-moy-ni-s
Proto-Italic *kommoinis
Old Latin comoinis
Latin commūnis
Old French comun
French commun
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti
Proto-Hellenic *-íd͏̌d͏̌ō
Ancient Greek -ῐ́ζω (-ĭ́zō)
Proto-Hellenic *-tās
Ancient Greek -τής (-tḗs)
Ancient Greek -ῐστής (-ĭstḗs)bor.
Latin -istalbor.
French -iste
French communiste
English communist
From French communiste, from commun (“common, communal”) + -iste (“-ist”). By surface analysis, commune + -ist.

ex.en: Communists took power in China in 1949.
ex.ja: 中国では1949年に共産党が政権を取った。

ex.en: I hope you'll never turn Communist.
ex.ja: 君が共産主義者にならないように希望する。

ex.en: I willingly join the Chinese Communist Party.
ex.ja: 喜んで中国共産党に入ります。

note.ja: com（共に）+ mun（務め）+ ist。財産を共有する主義（communism）の人 →「共産主義者」。

en: The act of complaining.
A grievance, problem, difficulty, or concern.

complaint.ety: From Middle English compleynte, from Anglo-Norman compleint, from Old French compleindre, eventually from Latin planctus (whence plaint).

ex.en: I am sick to death of your complaints.
ex.ja: 私はあなたのぐちには死ぬほどうんざりしている。

ex.en: The official could not deal with the complaint himself.
ex.ja: その役人は、自分自身でその苦情処理が出来なかった。

ex.en: I'm sick of listening to your complaints.
ex.ja: 君の愚痴を聞かされるのはうんざりだ。

en: The quality of being confident, not afraid or easily intimidated, but without being incautious or inconsiderate.
The ability to overcome one's fear, do or live things which one finds frightening.

courage.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱerd-
Proto-Indo-European *ḱḗr ~ *ḱr̥dés
Proto-Italic *kord
Latin cor n
Latin *corem
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos
Proto-Italic *-ātos
Latin -ātus
Proto-Indo-European *-ikos
Proto-Italic *-ikos
Latin -icus
Latin -āticus
Latin -āticum
Vulgar Latin *corāticum
Old French coragebor.
Middle English corage
English courage
From Middle English corage, from Old French corage (French courage), from Vulgar Latin *corāticum, from Latin cor (“heart”). Distantly related to cardiac (“of the heart”)

ex.en: He had the courage to decline the offer.
ex.ja: 彼は勇敢にもその申し出を断った。

ex.en: He showed courage in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険をかえりみず勇気を示した。

ex.en: Your courage will come out in a crisis.
ex.ja: いざとなれば勇気が湧いてくる。

note.ja: ラテン語 cor（心）から。cour + age。心の力 →「勇気」。

en: A method, device or medication that restores good health.
An act of healing or state of being healed; restoration to health after a disease, or to soundness after injury.
To restore to health.
To bring (a disease or its bad effects) to an end.

cure.ety: From Middle English cure, borrowed from Old French cure (“care, cure, healing, cure of souls”), from Latin cura (“care, medical attendance, cure”). Displaced native Old English hǣlu, but this survived as heal.

ex.en: Scientists haven't found a cure for cancer yet.
ex.ja: 科学者たちは未だに癌を完治させる方法を見出していない。

ex.en: This medicine will cure you of that disease.
ex.ja: この薬を飲めばその病気は治るでしょう。

ex.en: Cancer can be cured if discovered in time.
ex.ja: 発見が間に合えば、ガンは治療できる。

note.ja: ラテン語 cura（世話）から。世話をする →「治す・治療」。

en: In dire need (of something); having a dire need or desire.
Being filled with, or in a state of, despair; hopeless.
A person in desperate circumstances or who is at the point of desperation, such as a down-and-outer, addict, etc.

desperate.ety: From Middle English desperat(e) (“desperate”), borrowed from Latin dēspērātus, perfect passive participle of dēspērō (“to be without hope”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). The noun is derived from the adjective or from the Latin source through substantivization, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).

ex.en: He is in desperate search of further evidence.
ex.ja: 彼はもっと証拠がないかと、やっきになって捜している。

ex.en: He was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: 彼は名声を守ろうと必死だった。

ex.en: Tom was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: トムは自分の評判を守るのに必死だった。

en: The quality of being diverse or different; a difference or unlikeness.
A variety; diverse types or examples.

diversity.ety: From Middle English diversite, from Old French diversité, from Latin dīversitās, equivalent to diverse + -ity. Displaced native Old English mislīcnes.

ex.en: This forest is full of diversity.
ex.ja: この森は、多様性に富んでいます。

ex.en: Existing legislation does not take diversity of races into account.
ex.ja: 現行の法律は人種の多様性を考慮していない。

note.ja: di（離れて）+ vers（向ける）+ ity。別々の方向を向いていること →「多様性」。

en: The day or night before, usually used for holidays, such as Christmas Eve.
The period of time when something is just about to happen or to be introduced

eve.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider.
Proto-Germanic *ēbanþs
Proto-West Germanic *ābanþ
Old English ǣfen
Middle English evender.
Middle English eve
English eve
Inherited from Middle English eve, variant of even (itself from Old English ǣfen), with a pre-1200 loss of the terminal '-n'. See also the now archaic or poetic even (“evening”), from the same source.
In medieval Europe, days were considered to extend from sunset to sunset rather than midnight to midnight, so the night before a holiday was considered part of it, hence

ex.en: It is Eve that sets Adam on.
ex.ja: アダムをそそのかしたのはイブだ。

ex.en: Tom wanted to spend New Year's Eve with Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーと一緒に大晦日を過ごしたかった。

ex.en: That time was before New Year's Eve.
ex.ja: あの時は大晦日前だった。

en: The academic staff at schools, colleges, universities or not-for-profit research institutes, as opposed to the students or support staff.
A division of a university.

faculty.ety: From Middle English faculte (“power, property”), from Old French faculte, from Latin facultas (“capability, ability, skill, abundance, plenty, stock, goods, property; in Medieval Latin also a body of teachers”), another form of facilitas (“easiness, facility, etc.”), from facul, another form of facilis (“easy, facile”); see facile. Doublet of facility.

ex.en: He has the faculty to learn languages easily.
ex.ja: 彼は言葉を簡単に学ぶ能力をもっている。

ex.en: He has a faculty for making other people happy.
ex.ja: 彼は他人を楽しくさせる才能を持っている。

ex.en: She has a great faculty for music.
ex.ja: 彼女は音楽に優れた才能がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 facultas（できること）から。fac（する）。物事をする力 →「能力・機能」、（大学の）学部・教員。

en: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
The part of an output signal that is looped back into the input to control or modify a system.
To generate the high-frequency sound by allowing a speaker to cause vibration of the sound generator of a musical instrument connected by…
To provide informational feedback to.

feedback.ety:
Etymology tree
English feed
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-der.?
Proto-Germanic *baką
Proto-West Germanic *bak
Old English bæc
Middle English bak
English back
English feedback
From feed + back.

ex.en: Thank you for your valuable feedback.
ex.ja: 貴重なご意見をありがとうございます。

ex.en: We look forward to your feedback.
ex.ja: 僕らは君のフィードバックを楽しみしています。

ex.en: Please review the contents and provide any appropriate feedback.
ex.ja: 内容をご覧になり、適切なご意見をいただければ幸いです。

en: A person who fights; a combatant.
A warrior; a fighting soldier.

fighter.ety: From Middle English fightere, feghtere, from Old English feohtere. Equivalent to fight + -er.

ex.en: The fire fighters put out the fire.
ex.ja: 消防士は火事を消した。

ex.en: You're still a fire fighter, aren't you?
ex.ja: 今でも消防士なんでしょ？

ex.en: That fighter plane dropped a bomb.
ex.ja: その戦闘機は爆弾を投下した。

en: Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature.
To lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard.
A period of intensely cold weather.
A halt of a regular operation.

freeze.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *prews-der.
Proto-Germanic *-āną
Proto-Germanic *freusaną
Proto-West Germanic *freusan
Old English frēosan
Middle English fresen
English freeze
From Middle English fresen, from Old English frēosan (“to freeze”), from Proto-West Germanic *freusan, from Proto-Germanic *freusaną (“to freeze”), from Proto-Indo-European *prews- (“to freeze; frost”).
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian friis, friise, früüs (“to freeze”), Saterland Frisian fjoose, frjoze (“to freeze”), West Frisian frieze (“to freeze”), Central Franconian freese (“to freeze”), Cimbrian briizan, vrii

ex.en: How long can we keep this frozen food?
ex.ja: この冷凍食品はどのくらい保存できますか。

ex.en: What do you call it when water freezes?
ex.ja: 水が凍ったとき、それを何と呼びますか。

ex.en: She froze at the sight of the bear.
ex.ja: 彼女は熊を見かけて身がすくんだ。

en: Humankind; human beings as a group.
The human condition or nature.

humanity.ety: Inherited from Middle English humanyte, humanite, humanitye, from Old French humanité, from Latin hūmānitās. By surface analysis, human or humane + -ity. Partly displaced mankind, from Old English mancynn (literally “human race”).

ex.en: You should work in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 諸君は人類の利益のために働くべきだ。

ex.en: Nuclear weapons are a threat to all humanity.
ex.ja: 核兵器は全人類への脅威である。

ex.en: I'll do anything in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 人類のためになんでもするつもりだ。

en: The act of innovating; the introduction of something new, in customs, rites, etc.
A change effected by innovating; a change in customs.

innovation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French innovation, from Old French innovacion, from Late Latin innovatio, innovationem, from Latin innovo, innovatus. Morphologically innovate + -ion.

ex.en: A company that stifles innovation can't hope to grow very much.
ex.ja: 出る杭が打たれる会社じゃ、大きな成長は望めないね。

ex.en: Technological innovation brought about the rapid progress of the information industry.
ex.ja: 技術革新は情報産業に急速な進歩をもたらした。

ex.en: Open source is the engine that drives technological innovation.
ex.ja: オープンソースは技術革新をドライブするエンジンである。

en: A device used to produce music.
A means or agency for achieving an aspect.
To apply measuring devices.
To devise, conceive, cook up, plan.

instrument.ety:
From Middle English instrument, from Old French instrument, from Latin īnstrūmentum (“an implement, tool”),
From īnstruō (“build, construct; arrange”) + -mentum.

ex.en: You should on no condition touch these instruments.
ex.ja: どんなことがあってもこれらの器具に触れてはならない。

ex.en: You play a musical instrument, don't you?
ex.ja: あなたは楽器を演奏しますよね。

ex.en: Do you play a musical instrument?
ex.ja: 楽器をなにか演奏しますか。

note.ja: in（中に）+ stru（積む・備える）+ ment。備えておく道具 →「器具・楽器」。

en: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.
To envelop, wrap, cover.
A designated area of disturbed weather that is being monitored for potential tropical cyclone development.

invest.ety: Borrowed from Middle French investir or Medieval Latin investire, from Latin investio (“to clothe, cover”), from in- (“in, on”) + vestio (“to clothe, dress”), from vestis (“clothing”); see vest. The sense “to spend money etc.” probably via Italian investire, of the same root.

ex.en: The government should invest more money in industry.
ex.ja: 政府は産業にもっと多くの金を投資すべきだ。

ex.en: The Prime Minister is invested with incredible powers.
ex.ja: 首相は信じられないほどの権力を与えられている。

ex.en: The government should invest more money in agriculture.
ex.ja: 政府は農業にもっと投資するべきだ。

en: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length.
A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US).
To confine (someone) to a straitjacket.
To enclose or encase in a jacket or other covering.

jacket.ety: From Middle French jacquet, diminutive of Old French jaque.

ex.en: I want the same jacket as you're wearing.
ex.ja: 私はあなたが今着ているのと同じジャケットが欲しい。

ex.en: Do you have this jacket in different colors?
ex.ja: このジャケットの色違いはありますか。

ex.en: There was a black jacket on the book.
ex.ja: その本には黒いカバーがかかっていた。

en: Making, or having the power to make, a law or laws; lawmaking.
That branch of government which is responsible for making, or having the power to make, a law or laws.

legislative.ety:
Etymology tree
English legislate
Proto-Indo-European *-wós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.
Latin -īvus
Old French -ifbor.
Middle English -yf
English -ive
English legislative
From legislate + -ive.

en: Synonym of handbook.
A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
Performed with the hands.
Operated by means of the hands.

manual.ety: From Middle English manuel, from Old French manuel, from Late Latin manuāle (“handbook, manual”).

ex.en: He did hard manual labor through the day.
ex.ja: 彼はその日ずっと、つらい手仕事をやった。

ex.en: Manual labor is necessary in this company.
ex.ja: この会社では肉体労働が必要です。

ex.en: Do you drive a manual or automatic?
ex.ja: マニュアルを運転するの？それともオートマ？

note.ja: man（手）+ ual。手の →「手動の・手作業の」、手元に置く本 →「説明書」。

en: To fill.
To possess or use the time or capacity of; to engage the service of.

occupy.ety: From Middle English occupien, occupyen, borrowed from Old French occuper, from Latin occupāre (“to take possession of, seize, occupy, take up, employ”), from ob (“to, on”) + capiō (“to take”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“to seize, grab”). Doublet of occupate, now obsolete.

ex.en: The meeting room is occupied at the moment.
ex.ja: 会議室は現在使用中です。

ex.en: The city was soon occupied by the soldiers.
ex.ja: その市はやがて兵隊によって占領された。

ex.en: He was fully occupied with his writing.
ex.ja: 彼は著述に励んでいた。

en: Continuing, permanent, lasting.
Presently or currently happening; being in progress.
Something that is going on; a happening.

ongoing.ety: From on + going, related to the phrasal verb go on.

ex.en: Development is slow, but ongoing.
ex.ja: 細々とだが開発は続いている。

ex.en: The investigation is ongoing.
ex.ja: その調査は進行中です。

ex.en: The process is ongoing.
ex.ja: 現在、処理中です。

en: A person or organisation that operates a device, system, service, etc.
A telecommunications facilitator whose job is to connect or otherwise assist callers.

operator.ety: Borrowed from Latin operātor, from operor (“work, labour”). Equivalent to operate + -or.

ex.en: The operator put me through to New York.
ex.ja: 交換手が電話をニューヨークへつないでくれた。

ex.en: Operator, I'm trying to get through to Boston.
ex.ja: 交換台、ボストンに電話しようとしているんですが。

ex.en: This is the operator. Which extension would you like?
ex.ja: 交換手です。内線番号をどうぞ。

en: Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental.
Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person).

painful.ety: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).

ex.en: It's painful to keep sitting for hours.
ex.ja: 何時間も座っているのは苦痛だ。

ex.en: There's nothing more painful than losing one's loved child.
ex.ja: 愛する我が子を失うことほど辛いことはない。

ex.en: Sometimes, life is difficult and painful.
ex.ja: 時には人生が辛くて難しい。

en: The act of preparing or getting ready.
The state of being prepared; readiness.

preparation.ety: From Middle English preparacion, from Middle French preparacion, from Latin praeparatio, praeparationem. Morphologically prepare + -ation.

ex.en: In preparation, clean the bath and fill it.
ex.ja: お風呂洗って、入れといてね。

ex.en: We failed due to a lack of preparation.

ex.ja: この本は非常に楽しく読めます。

ex.ja: ホラー映画を見ることに楽しみを見いだす人もいる。

ex.ja: 英語の学習から大いに利益を得るだろう。

Any force acting in opposition to the motion of an object.

To proceed heavily, laboriously, or slowly; to advance with weary effort; to go on lingeringly.

ex.ja: ポールはよく重いツールをずるずる引きずる。

en: To instruct or train.

educate.ety: From Middle English educaten, from educat(e) (“educated”, also used as the past participle of educaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), from Latin ēducātus, the perfect passive participle of ēducō (“(of a child, physically or mentally) to bring up, train, nourish; (of a person in learning or art) to rear, educate, train; (plants or animals) to nourish, support, or produce”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), further from an intensive/frequentative formed on ēducō (“lead out, draw out; to raise up, erect”) + -ō.

ex.en: She was educated in the United States.
ex.ja: 彼女は米国で教育を受けた。

ex.en: He was educated at a public school.
ex.ja: 彼は公立学校で教育を受けた。

ex.en: All educated Americans, first or last, go to Europe.
ex.ja: 全ての教養あるアメリカ人は最初かまたは最後にヨーロッパに行く。

en: Allowed to and meeting the necessary conditions required to participate in or be chosen for something.
Worthy of being chosen (for marriage).
One who is eligible.

eligible.ety: From Middle French eligible, from Latin eligibilis, from ēligō (“to select, to choose”).

ex.en: Tom says that he isn't eligible to vote.
ex.ja: トムは彼には投票権がないと言う。

ex.en: She is not eligible for marriage.
ex.ja: 彼女は、結婚の資格はない。

ex.en: Mr Frost is eligible for the post.
ex.ja: フロスト氏はその地位につく資格がある。

en: The act, manner or style of executing (actions, maneuvers, performances).
The state of being accomplished.

execution.ety: From Old French execution (c.1360), from Latin exsecutiō, an agent noun from exsequor (“to follow out”), from ex (“out”) + sequor (“follow”). Equivalent to execute + -ion.

en: The cardinal number occurring after forty-nine and before fifty-one.
A banknote or coin with a denomination of 50.
A batsman's score of at least 50 runs and less than 100 runs.

ex.ja: その男は５０年にわたってその国を支配した。

ex.ja: この寒さは５０年ぶりのひどさでした。

ex.ja: 昨年私は少なくとも５０本は映画を見た。

en: One who follows, comes after another.
Something that comes after another thing.

follower.ety: From Middle English folwer, folwere, folewer, from Old English folgere (“follower; attendant; disciple”), equivalent to follow + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Foulger, West Frisian folger, Dutch volger, German Folger, Swedish följare.

ex.en: How many followers do you have on Twitter?
ex.ja: Twitterのフォロワーって何人ぐらいいるの？

ex.en: She is a follower of Freud.
ex.ja: 彼女はフロイトの信奉者だ。

ex.en: On the religious side, the decision caused serious dissension among followers.
ex.ja: 宗教的側面では、その決定は信者たちに深刻な分裂をもたらした。

A stock character typified by unintelligence, naïveté or lucklessness, usually as a form of comic relief; often used as a source of insig…
To trick; to deceive.
To act in an idiotic manner; to act foolishly.
Foolish.

From Middle English fol (“fool”), from Old French fol (cf. modern French fou (“mad”)) from Latin follis. Doublet of fals and follis. Displaced native Old English dwæs.

ex.en: If I am a fool, you are another.
ex.ja: 私が馬鹿なら君もそうだ。

ex.en: He is, so to speak, a learned fool.
ex.ja: 彼はいわば学者ばかだ。

ex.en: He is a wise fool, so to speak.
ex.ja: 彼はいわば賢い愚か者だ。

en: A support structure comprising joined parts or conglomerated particles and intervening open spaces of similar or larger size.
The arrangement of support beams that represent a building's general shape and size.

ex.en: The framework of the new building is slowly taking form.
ex.ja: 新しい建物の骨組みが徐々に姿を見せてきている。

ex.en: The building will be made of concrete on a steel framework.
ex.ja: その建物は鋼鉄の骨組みにコンクリートで作られる事になっている。

en: The right to vote at a public election or referendum; see: suffrage.
A right or privilege officially granted to a person, a group of people, or a company by a government.
To confer certain powers on; grant a franchise to; authorize.
To give to others the rights to sell or distribute (goods or services).

franchise.ety: From Middle English franchise, fraunchise, from Old French franchise (“freedom”), a derivative of franc (“free”). More at frank.

en: Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
The harness, trappings etc. of a horse, hawk, or other animal.

furniture.ety: From Middle French fourniture (“a supply, or the act of furnishing”), from fournir (“to furnish”).

ex.en: The furniture in this office is really modern.
ex.ja: この事務所の家具はなかなか近代的だ。

ex.ja: 部屋の中には１つの家具も残っていない。

ex.en: There is too much furniture in the house.
ex.ja: その家には家具がたくさんありすぎる。

en: To include as a constituent part or functionality.
To join a group or an environment harmoniously; to make oneself fit in.

integrate.ety: First attested in the 1450's as an adjective, first attested in 1638 as a verb; from Middle English integrat(e) (“intact, whole”), borrowed from Latin integrātus, perfect passive participle of integrō (“to make whole, renew, repair, begin again”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from integer (“whole, fresh”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). ex.ja: このプロダクトはインテリジェント総合情報システムです。

ex.ja: その学校は、中・高一貫校だということを頭の片隅にでも入れておいて下さい。

ex.en: We are aiming for an integrated development zone that combines business and industrial quarters.
ex.ja: 工業区と商業区が一体となった総合的な開発区を目指しております。

To spray out of a container.
To spray with liquid from a container.
Propelled by turbine engines.

To fasten or encircle something with a loop.

ex.ja: 私たちにも情報を共有していただければ助かります。

ex.ja: 今度の風邪には本当にまいったよ。

Abroad.
Across a sea; to an area across a sea.

overseas.ety: From earlier oversea, equivalent to oversea + -s. Compare West Frisian oerseesk, Dutch overzees, German Übersee, Danish oversøisk.

ex.ja: 父は来週海外へ行く予定だ。

ex.en: I am working in the Overseas Operations Division.
ex.ja: 私は海外事業部で働いています。

ex.en: I haven't heard from my son who's overseas.

en: A substance used to polish.
Cleanliness; smoothness, shininess.
To shine; to make a surface very smooth or shiny by rubbing, cleaning, or grinding.
To refine; remove imperfections from.

polish.ety: From Middle English polishen, from Old French poliss-, stem of some of the conjugated forms of polir, from Latin polīre (“to polish, make smooth”), from Proto-Indo-European *pelh₂- (“to drive, strike, thrust”), from the notion of fulling cloth.

ex.en: When did the Japanese start eating polished rice?
ex.ja: いつから日本人は精白米を食べるようになったのですか？

ex.en: I got him to polish my shoes.
ex.ja: 私は彼に靴を磨いてもらった。

ex.en: The diamond in this ring is polished.
ex.ja: この指輪のダイヤは研磨してある。

en: An act of recommending.
That which is recommended.

recommendation.ety: From Middle English recommendacioun, from Anglo-Norman recomendacion, from Medieval Latin recommendatio. By surface analysis, recommend + -ation.

ex.en: I've added my recommendations to improve the situation.
ex.ja: 状況を改善するための提案を付け加えておきました。

ex.en: The recommendation from my boss made all the difference.
ex.ja: 課長からもらった推薦状が物を言った。

ex.en: My teacher wrote a recommendation for me.
ex.ja: 先生は私のために推薦状を書いた。

en: To get back, to regain (a physical thing; in astronomy and navigation, sight of a thing or a signal).
To salvage, to extricate, to rescue (a thing or person).
A position of holding a firearm during exercises, whereby the lock is at shoulder height and the sling facing out.

recover.ety:

ex.ja: 早く本調子になるといいね。

ex.en: The patient will soon recover from his illness.
ex.ja: 患者はまもなく病気が治るだろう。

en: To make something loose.
To become loose.

relax.ety: From Middle English relaxen, from Old French relaxer, from Latin relaxāre (“relax, loosen, open”), from re- (“back”) + laxāre (“loosen”), from laxus (“loose, free”). By surface analysis, re- + lax (“open, free, loose”).

ex.ja: 彼はギターを弾いているとリラックスできる。

To depend; to be dependent upon.

ex.ja: 彼は信頼できる人ではない。

Uncommon; unusual.

To destroy or kill (a human being or an animal); specifically (sciences), to kill (an animal) for a scientific experiment or test.

To replace or supplant someone in order vis-à-vis an office, position, or title.

succeed.ety:
From Old French succeder, from Latin succedere (“to go under, go from under, come under, approach, follow, take the place of, receive by succession, prosper, be successful”).
Partly displaced English speed, of which the original sense “to succeed” only survives in a few fossilized expressions such as Godspeed.

ex.ja: 彼はその実験に成功することを確信している。

ex.en: Try as they may, they will never succeed.
ex.ja: どんなに努力しても、彼らは絶対成功しないだろう。

ex.en: You are sure to succeed, whatever you do.
ex.ja: 何をしようとも、君は必ず成功する。

note.ja: suc（下から・次に）+ ceed（進む）。次に進む →「後を継ぐ・成功する」。

en: A rehearsal of what has occurred; narrative; discourse; statement; history; story.
A number told or counted off; a reckoning by count; an enumeration.

tale.ety:
From Middle English tale, from Old English talu (“tale, series, calculation”), from Proto-West Germanic *talu, from Proto-Germanic *talō (“calculation, number”), from Proto-Indo-European *del- (“to reckon, count”).
Cognate with West Frisian taal (“speech, language”), Dutch taal (“language, speech”), German Zahl (“number, figure”), Danish tale (“speech”), Icelandic tala (“speech, talk, discourse, number, figure”), Latin dolus (“guile, deceit, fraud”), Ancient Greek δόλος (dólos, “wile, bait”), Albanian ndjell (“to lure”), Northern Kurdish til (“finger”), Old Armenian տող (toł, “row”). The long ton of 2240 pounds (about 1016 kg), 20 hundredweights of 112 pounds avoirdupois each.

ex.ja: 彼は茶の販売予定は十トンです。

en: One who enters into, or offers themselves for, any service of their own free will, especially when done without pay.
One who enters into military service voluntarily (but who, when in service, is subject to discipline and regulations like other soldiers)…
To enlist oneself as a volunteer.
To do or offer to do something voluntarily.

volunteer.ety: Borrowed from Middle French voluntaire, from Latin voluntārius (“willing, voluntary”); or from voluntary + -eer.

ex.en: The babies are taken care of by volunteers.
ex.ja: その赤ちゃんはボランティアによって世話される。

ex.en: There are people who engage in volunteer work.
ex.ja: ボランティアの仕事に従事する者もいる。

ex.en: I'd like to volunteer to go with Tom.
ex.ja: トムと一緒にボランティアに行きたいんです。

en: The devotion accorded to a deity or to a sacred object.
The adoration (or latria) owed to God alone, as greater than the hyperdulia that is given to Saint Mary only and the veneration (or dulia…
To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.
To honour with extravagant love and extreme submission, as a lover; to adore; to idolize.

worship.ety: Inherited from Middle English worschipe /worthschipe, inherited from Old English weorþsċiepe. Cognate with Scots worschip (“worship”). By surface analysis, wor(th) + -ship.

ex.en: It is money that many people worship most.
ex.ja: 多くの人が最も崇拝するものはお金である。

ex.en: He is worshiped as a god by everyone.
ex.ja: 彼は皆から神のようにあがめられている。

ex.en: They worshipped him as a hero.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼を英雄として崇拝した。

en: Having worth, merit, or value.
Admirable or honourable.
A distinguished or eminent person.
a good, wise and virtuous person.
To render or treat as worthy.

worthy.ety: From Middle English worthy, wurthi, from Old English *weorþiġ (“worthy”), equivalent to worth + -y. Cognate with Dutch waardig (“worthy”), Middle Low German werdig (“worthy”), German würdig (“worthy”), Swedish värdig (“worthy”), Icelandic verðugur (“worthy”).

ex.ja: 彼の提案は考慮に値する。

ex.en: The offer is worthy of being considered.
ex.ja: その申し出は考慮に値する。

ex.en: He isn't worthy to take the lead.
ex.ja: 彼は指導者たるにふさわしくない人だ。

en: A summons to arms, as on the approach of an enemy.
Any sound or information intended to give notice of approaching danger; a warning sound to arouse attention; a warning of danger.
To call to arms for defense.
To give (someone) notice of approaching danger or necessary action; to rouse to vigilance; to put on the alert.

alarm.ety: From Middle English alarme, alarom, borrowed from Middle French alarme, itself from Old Italian all'arme! (“to arms!, to the weapons!”), ultimately from Latin arma (“arms, weapons”).

ex.en: I set my alarm to go off at 2:30.
ex.ja: 2時半にアラームが鳴るようにセットした。

ex.en: The alarm clock is set for 5 a.m.
ex.ja: 目覚ましは午前５時にセットされる。

ex.en: The news of the accident caused public alarm.
ex.ja: その事故のニュースで人々は不安になった。

A low spectrum of sound tones.
A section of a musical group that produces low-pitched sound, lower than the baritone and tenor.
To sound in a deep tone.

Characterised by bloodshed.
To stain with blood.
To draw blood from (one's opponent) in a fight.

To take in needed gases and expel waste gases in a similar way.

The whole buttocks and pelvic region that includes one's private parts.
To join at the butt, end, or outward extremity; to terminate; to be bounded; to abut.

A distinguishing feature of a person or thing, a part of mental or physical behavior.

A production or creation made by collaborating.

en: The thought process of considering, of taking multiple or specified factors into account (with of being the main corresponding adposition).
Something considered as a reason or ground for a (possible) decision.

consideration.ety: From Middle English consideracioun, from Old French consideracion, from Latin cōnsīderātiō. By surface analysis, consider + -ation.

ex.en: The price did not enter into our consideration.
ex.ja: 私たちは物価を注目しなかった。

ex.en: Taking everything into consideration, he bought the car.
ex.ja: すべてのことを考慮して彼はその車を買った。

ex.en: We should have taken the schedule into consideration.
ex.ja: 私たちは日程を考慮に入れるべきだった。

en: Essential or decisive for determining the outcome or future of something; extremely important; vital.

crucial.ety:
1706, from French crucial, a medical term for ligaments of the knee (which cross each other), from Latin crux, crucis (“cross”) (English crux), from the Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to turn, to bend”).
The meaning “decisive, critical” is extended from a logical term, Instantias Crucis, adopted by Francis Bacon in his influential Novum Organum (1620); the notion is of cross fingerboard signposts at forking roads, thus a requirement to choose.

ex.en: Why isn't Tom here at this crucial moment?
ex.ja: なんでこの肝心な時にトムがいないんだよ！

ex.en: It is crucial for world peace.
ex.ja: それは、世界の平和のためにとても大切なことです。

ex.en: We are facing a crucial time.
ex.ja: 今が我々にとって一番大切な時だ。

en: Relying upon; depending upon.
Having a probability that is affected by the outcome of a separate event.
A person who relies on another for support or sustenance, particularly financial support.
An element in phrase or clause structure that is not the head. Includes complements, modifiers and determiners.

dependent.ety: From Middle English dependaunt, dependent, from Middle French dependant (present participle of dependre (“to depend”)) and Latin dēpendēns (present participle of dēpendeō (“to depend”)). By surface analysis, depend + -ent.

ex.en: Though 38, he is still dependent on his parents.
ex.ja: 彼は３８歳なのに両親に頼りきりです。

ex.en: The boy is totally dependent on his parents.
ex.ja: その男の子は両親に完全に頼っている。

ex.en: Japan is dependent on foreign countries for oil.
ex.ja: 日本は石油を外国に依存している。

note.ja: de（下に）+ pend（ぶら下がる）+ ent。下にぶら下がっている →「頼っている・依存した」。

ex.en: He was equipped for a trip.

Serving to be experimented upon; used in an experiment.
The subject of an experiment.

ex.en: Our experimental results left something to be desired.

ex.ja: 実験方法に欠陥があるに違いない。

ex.en: Something is wrong with the experimental apparatus.
ex.ja: 実験用器具が故障している。

Electronics or software that separates unwanted signals (for example noise) from wanted signals or that attenuates selected frequencies.
To sort, sift, or isolate.
To diffuse; to cause to be less concentrated or focused.

filter.ety: From Middle English filtre, from Medieval Latin filtrum (compare also Old French feutre (“felt; filter”)), from Frankish *filtir, from Proto-West Germanic *felt. See felt. Doublet of phin.

ex.ja: 新しい整水器、買ってもらったんだ。

ex.ja: 新しい整水器、買ってもらったんだ。

ex.en: This store uses a water filter.
ex.ja: 当店の水は浄水器を使用しています。

en: Any of the collections of many millions or billions of stars, galactic dust, black holes, etc. existing as independent and coherent syste…
An assemblage of things or people seen as luminous or brilliant.
To furnish with galaxies.

galaxy.ety: From Middle English galaxye, galaxie, from Old French galaxie, from Latin galaxias, from Ancient Greek γαλαξίας (galaxías, “Milky Way”), shortening of γαλαξίας κύκλος (galaxías kúklos, “milky circle”), from γάλα (gála, “milk”).

ex.en: There are many galaxies in the universe.
ex.ja: 宇宙にはたくさんの銀河がある。

ex.ja: 私たちは銀河に住んでいます。

ex.en: There are innumerable stars in the galaxy.
ex.ja: 銀河系には無数の星がある。

A spherical model of Earth or of another planet.
To become spherical.
To make spherical.

globe.ety: From late Middle English globe, from Middle French globe, from Old French globe, borrowed from Latin globus. Doublet of globus.

ex.ja: 私は世界中を旅行する。

That which swallows irretrievably; a whirlpool; a sucking eddy.
To engulf.
To award a degree to somebody who has only just passed sufficiently.

gulf.ety: From Middle English gulf, goulf, golf, from Old French golf, from Italian golfo, from Late Latin colfos, from Ancient Greek κόλπος (kólpos, “bosom, gulf”), of obscure origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *kʷelp- (“to curve, arch”).

An especially significant or interesting detail or event or period of time.

To be a highlight of.

The state of someone’s mind at the time of committing an offence.
Firmly fixed or concentrated on something.

judgment.ety: From Middle English juggement, borrowed from Old French jugement, from Late Latin iūdicāmentum, from Latin iūdicō. Partially displaced doom. By surface analysis, judge + -ment.

ex.ja: その判断は双方に対して大変公正なものである。

A minor nobleman with an honourable military rank who had served as a page and squire.
To confer knighthood upon.
To promote (a pawn) to a knight.

knight.ety: From Middle English knight, knyght, kniht, from Old English cniht (“boy; servant, knight”), from Proto-West Germanic *kneht.

Brought to a state of complete readiness.
To proceed toward maturity: full development or completion (either of concrete or of abstract things, e.g. plans, judgments, qualities).
To attain maturity, to become mature or ripe.

mature.ety: From late Middle English mature, from Middle French mature, from Latin mātūrus. Doublet of maduro. Partially displaced ripe, from Old English rīpe (“ripe, mature”).

ex.ja: 私は真の大人の女性に会いたいと思った。
